I’m starting a **greenfield** project on my **Mac desktop** to **track and visualize usage** across:

- **Cursor** (IDE / agent usage — whatever we can read locally: logs, sqlite, exports, etc.)

- **Gemini** (Google AI Studio or API usage — only if we can do it without sketchy scraping; document limits)

**Implementation:** I’m fine with either a **simple local web app** (browser + local server) **or Electron** — choose whichever gets a **credible v1** faster with **clear upgrade paths**. Explain the tradeoff in two sentences, then proceed.

## Product v1 (adjust scope as you discover what’s readable)

- **Discover** where each tool stores **usage-relevant** data on macOS (paths, formats, permissions). **Read-only**; don’t modify vendor apps.
- **Ingest** into something queryable (SQLite or JSON — pick simple).
- **Minimal UI**: dashboard or table — totals over time, last session, rough token/cost estimates **only if** we have real signals; otherwise show **honest “unknown”** and what’s missing.
- **Privacy:** offline-first; document what never leaves the machine.
